title: Roadmap
description: A roadmap page for Star Atlas that clarifies what is playable now, what is expanding next, and how long-term ambition is communicated without hype or confusion.
heroTitle: Status should be understandable in one glance.
heroSummary: This roadmap template replaces vague launch-state language with a calmer frame: what exists now, what is expanding next, and what remains part of the long arc of the universe.
utilityLine: Avoid quarter-heavy timelines here unless they can be maintained rigorously. The structure is designed to stay useful even when exact dates evolve.

heroMedia.label: Trajectory
heroMedia.caption: A roadmap should reduce uncertainty, not create more of it.

heroPanel.title: The roadmap now favors clarity over theater.
heroPanel.body: No countdowns, no brittle urgency signals, and no contradictory state labels. The page is designed to help visitors understand momentum without overpromising.

sections.heading: Frame the product around momentum, not hype.

items.title: Playable browser and market surfaces
items.body: Lead with the parts of the product that are already accessible and meaningful for first-touch visitors.

items.title: Broader gameplay and command expansion
items.body: Use this band for the layers that are actively deepening and deserve clear expectation-setting.

items.title: The full long-range universe vision
items.body: Reserve this space for ambition, but keep it obviously separate from immediate product reality.

sections.heading: What this page should never do again.

cards.title: Do not compete with the hero
cards.body: The roadmap should clarify state, not bury it under repeated CTAs or utility chrome.

cards.title: Use one consistent product-state vocabulary
cards.body: If the product is playable in some surfaces and expanding in others, say that plainly and consistently everywhere.

cards.title: Remove brittle urgency signals
cards.body: Countdowns, old campaign artifacts, and unclear launch labels make the product feel less premium.

sections.heading: How to keep roadmap messaging trustworthy.

items.question: Why use now, next, and later instead of dated quarters everywhere?
items.answer: Because this structure stays useful when schedules shift and avoids the trust erosion that comes from stale date promises.

items.question: What should be mirrored on the homepage?
items.answer: Only the high-level status summary. The detailed explanation lives here so the homepage stays calm and focused.

finalCta.title: Move from status clarity into action.
finalCta.text: Launch the browser experience, visit the newsroom, or continue into the game and economy pages with a clearer understanding of product state.
